text: Cornerstone channel is live. Keep it candid in here but remember everything is discoverable. First thing we need is a backlog number we can defend to the regulator.
Quick first-pass on the backlog: ~1,400 alerts and on a fast look basically all of them could be SAR-eligible. Sending a prelim memo. Caveat: not risk-tiered yet, done under time pressure.
Let's NOT run with 'all 1,400 SAR-eligible' — that's an alarmed read, not a triaged one. Tier it first. I don't want that number leaving the room.

Backlog report is out: ~1,400 uninvestigated, inclusive of auto-closed. The prelim 'all SAR-eligible' line is retracted — on triage the great majority is low-risk. SAR candidates concentrate in the ~180 high-risk queue.
Heads up, the Sentinel dashboard says ~900 open, not 1,400. Which number do we use?

Both are real, they count different things. Dashboard's ~900 = live analyst queue only, EXCLUDES auto-closed. Our ~1,400 INCLUDES auto-closed because the system closing an alert by itself isn't a review. For the MRA we use the inclusive 1,400. The 900 understates what we're accountable for.

Audit note: Sentinel's selling 40% FP reduction and I'm seeing that number creep into staffing assumptions. Model Risk validated ~15% on OUR data and even that isn't robust. Don't plan around the vendor number.
Agree. Validated 15%-not-robust governs, not the 40% brochure. Stripping it from the capacity plan.
Filed the monitoring data-gap memo. ~3 weeks during the cutover where the monitoring feed wasn't complete and scenarios didn't fire on the affected feeds. That's Finding 1 in the flesh.
Pushing back on the framing — core reconciliation is clean, NO data loss, balances tie to the penny. I don't want a memo that reads as 'the bank lost data.'

Greg, ledger whole ≠ monitoring feed complete. Different controls. I'm not saying we lost transactions, I'm saying monitoring coverage was incomplete for ~3 weeks. Both can be true. We still have to re-run monitoring over the window.
Regulator follow-up landed. Flat $10k threshold is 'inadequate,' they expect risk-based. Threshold debate moves to Friday, steering decides.

Flagging from Retail: dropping the floor to $5k is going to light up a lot of ordinary consumer activity. That's real customer friction — holds, outreach, abandoned transactions. I'll bring numbers Friday.

Heard, Lena. That's why it's risk-based, not flat $5k — low-risk consumer accounts get a higher effective floor. But coverage can't lose to friction; the appetite statement is explicit on that. Friday.
Migration risk review done. We're going phased, not big-bang. Another single-weekend cutover during an open MRA is too much monitoring-coverage risk. Plan gets reissued.
Governance change incoming: program ownership moves to a remediation PMO under Dana. Priya keeps the fincrime workstreams. This is about the Finding-3 accountability line, not delivery.
Steering approved: $5k risk-based threshold AND the PMO governance model. Both binding. Threshold v2 and the governance memo go out this week. Good work everyone.
